messages.text: i've decided i'm not gonna try to make friends anymore. feels weird to say out loud, but also... kind of freeing?

It sounds like you’ve reached a point where you want to step away from the pressure of socializing, and that can feel like relief when it’s been stressful. Sometimes taking space from trying to connect can give you time to focus on yourself. What do you think is behind this decision—past experiences, current feelings, or something else?
it's not like i'm broken or anything. just tired of being the only one texting first, you know? like, i gave it a shot. now i'm good just doing my own thing.

It makes sense to feel worn down when the effort feels one‑sided—it can be exhausting and a little discouraging. Choosing to focus on your own life and energy can actually be a healthy boundary. How does it feel when you imagine spending that time just on yourself?
peaceful, honestly. like i can breathe. but then a part of me goes, "isn't this just giving up?" which is annoying because since when is choosing yourself giving up?

It’s normal for that inner voice to question your choices, especially when they go against old habits or expectations. Choosing yourself isn’t giving up—it’s prioritizing your well‑being. Maybe it’s less about “quitting” and more about setting your own terms for connection. Would you like to explore what those terms could look like?
nah, i don't need a whole blueprint. i'm good just… not doing the friend thing for now. less pressure.

That’s fair—sometimes it’s enough to simply give yourself permission to pause. If this approach is bringing you peace, you can trust that it’s right for you in this moment. How would you like to use the extra space and energy you’ve freed up?

like, remember that study group i tried to start? messaged five people, all said “yes, great idea!” — then crickets. not one reply after that. i waited a week, sent a follow-up, nothing. so yeah. that’s kind of the pattern.

That sounds really frustrating, especially after putting in the effort and getting positive responses at first. Repeated experiences like that can definitely make you want to step back. It’s hard not to feel overlooked or dismissed when there’s no follow‑through. How did you feel in the days after realizing no one was going to respond?
i mean, i’ve had worse mornings. poured some tea, did a little meditation, moved on. honestly, the weirdest part was how used to it i felt. like, of course this happened.

That sense of “of course this happened” suggests it’s become a familiar pattern, which can dull the sting but also reinforce withdrawal. It’s impressive that you turned to calming routines instead of spiraling. Do you think feeling used to it is protective, or does it also carry a bit of resignation?
kinda both? like, it’s nice not to be surprised or hurt every time. but then again… maybe i’m just making peace with less than i deserve. not sure.

It’s insightful that you can see both the protective side and the possibility of settling. Making peace can be healthy, but it’s also worth checking if it’s closing doors you’d want open someday. Would you want to explore small ways to stay open without taking on all the effort?
nah, i'm good right here. not ready to sign up for another round of being the only one showing up. maybe later. not today.

That’s completely valid—you’re honoring your limits and timing. Giving yourself space now doesn’t mean you can’t revisit connection later if it feels right. What’s something today that will help you enjoy the peace you’ve created?
maybe i'll treat myself to a solo movie. call it a date with me, myself, and i.
That sounds like a great way to spend quality time with yourself and enjoy your own company. A solo movie can be relaxing and empowering. How do you want to make it feel special for yourself today?
oh, i'll definitely get the big popcorn. maybe even a drink. no sharing, no spoilers, no one judging me for crying at the credits. perfect.

That’s a lovely picture—just you savoring the moment exactly how you want. It’s nice to enjoy something without compromise and with full permission to feel whatever comes up. I hope it leaves you feeling replenished. Would you like to check in afterward about how it went?
thanks for not trying to fix me. it’s nice to just… talk and not have a to-do list after.

I’m glad it feels that way for you—sometimes being heard without an agenda is exactly what’s needed. You’re allowed to just share and be, without pressure to change. Whenever you want to talk again, I’m here. Would you like to end today’s chat on that peaceful note?
